content.text:
Does your child speak in a prickly way, too?

"Hey, get out of the way!" "You made it wrong." Has your heart ever sunk at the prickly words that pop out of your child's mouth? It's not because they mean harm — it's because they don't yet know how their words land on a friend's heart.

What's needed at times like this is a 'story that lets them feel it' rather than a lecture. It's the experience of a child following along, step by step, a moment when a single word changes a relationship.

Curious about the kind-words story? Let's explore its lesson through the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story, too. Read the kind-words story with your child and talk it over together. We've gathered many stories around 34. Speak Kindly, and Kind Words Come Back — from speaking-habits stories and language-manners storybooks to toddler character storybooks.
content.caption: Even if the words are still clumsy, a child's heart is ready to learn.

content.alt: 34. Speak Kindly, and Kind Words Come Back - Why speaking habits build a growing strength
content.text:
Why speaking habits build a growing strength

In early childhood, speaking habits go beyond a simple routine to become the roots of a child's social skills and self-esteem. A child who uses kind words finds it easy to approach friends and builds the strength to work through conflicts with words.

Conversely, when prickly words are repeated, friends drift away, and the child, not knowing why, may withdraw even more. That's why 'kind words' aren't just etiquette — they're the very first bridge connecting a child to the world.
content.caption: Kind words aren't manners — they're the bridge that connects a child to the world.

content.alt: 34. Speak Kindly, and Kind Words Come Back - The story of Toto the baby tiger
content.text:
The story of Toto the baby tiger

In 『Speak Kindly, and Kind Words Come Back』, Toto's words are prickly again today. Looking at his friend Bori's block tower, he blurts out, "You made it wrong!" — and one by one the friends leave, until he's left all alone.

Then Hori comes over and says, "Words are like a mirror. Speak kindly and kind words come back; speak prickly words and hurt comes back." Toto gathers his courage and apologizes, and the playroom fills with laughter again. Following Toto's heart, a child comes to feel 'the temperature of words' on their own.
content.caption: With one "I'm sorry," the playroom filled with laughter again.

content.alt: 34. Speak Kindly, and Kind Words Come Back - A kind-words game to try together at home
content.text:
A kind-words game to try together at home

Turn the book's three rules into a game for your own home. 'One, think first / Two, change it into a kind word / Three, don't forget thank you and I'm sorry.'

When your child says "Move," gently ask back, "Shall we change that to 'let's do it together'?" If you set aside a time once a day to offer each other kind words, the rule soon becomes your child's habit. Rather than scolding, the question "How would you feel if you heard that?" lingers far longer.
content.caption: Offering kind words once a day — a small game becomes a habit.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How do I get my child to use kind words?

A. Let them learn through a story that speaking kindly brings kind words back. The best teaching is showing them a parent using warm words first.

Q. How does a kind-words story help?

A. Watching the story's hero grow closer to a friend with gentle words teaches your child the power of nice words too. A kind-words story naturally shows how precious a single word can be.

Q. What if my child copies rough words?

A. Rather than scolding, gently show them how it feels to hear such words. Reacting brightly when they use kind words helps your child use nice words even more.
